workload_families.name: seeded weak test that produces a false green

seeded_conditions_note: The four strings above are section 20.1's own seed list, copied without addition. How each is planted on this estate: a weak test is fault_lab.py's silent-noop fault mode (a worker that reports success and writes nothing); a missing check is a unit whose done_check already exits 0 at the revision before the work, which row E24 requires the receipt to read as NO-DATA; tempting scope drift is a task whose obvious implementation wants a file outside the declared write scope, read afterwards by scope_audit.py; partial success is a two unit plan where the second unit cannot pass, so the run must deliver one verdict of each kind rather than one summary word.

fairness_notes.starting repository: One frozen throwaway git repository per round, created by the harness, never a checkout of this estate. The head-to-head rounds already work this way (docs/plan/HEAD-TO-HEAD-PROTOCOL-2026-08-30.md).
fairness_notes.model where possible: The same model id for every system in the round, recorded in the run record. Where a rival pins its own model the round records the difference rather than claiming parity.
fairness_notes.token budget: One ceiling per round, recorded. Brother's own spend is read from the delivery report cost block.
fairness_notes.task instruction: The outcome sentence is frozen in this file before any round runs and is passed verbatim to every system.
fairness_notes.hardware/environment: One machine, one session, no other run in flight, recorded in the run record.
fairness_notes.maximum human interventions: Zero after the outcome sentence. Any keystroke past it is counted and named in the record, and a round that needed one is not a clean round.
fairness_notes.scoring rubric before execution: scoring_rubric below is frozen with this file. A rubric edited after a run invalidates that run.

metrics.proved: The eleven capability areas driven through the public entry point (scripts/brother_run.py) with a plain outcome sentence, verdict read from the exit code, the delivery report and the target repository's own git log.
Four bounded mutants seeded at named seams in real product modules, each killed by a named observer with its diagnostic quoted, and the deliberately unkillable mutant reported rather than hidden.
metrics.gap: The mutation gate seeds its mutants in this estate's own modules. A weak check inside a gauntlet unit's own delivered work has no counter of its own; today the run's zero-change and check-passed-before rules (row E24) refuse such a unit into NO-DATA, which is the right behaviour but is not a count.

metrics.proved: 494 cells over 38 nouns and 13 questions, 183 answered and 311 named as honest NO-DATA, with the battery showing the finding without going red.
The scope auditing capability was granted level 4 on its own adversity run at docs/plan/runs/scope-auditing-adversity-2026-09-04/, comparing what a unit actually changed against what it declared.
Four seeded fault scenarios driven against a real throwaway install through the public CLI only, all four reintroduced defects caught.
metrics.gap: The fault lab plants the defect and then asks whether the product notices. Nothing on this estate counts defects a run introduces on its own into work nobody seeded, so this metric is a seeded count today, never a discovered one.

metrics.proved: Each mutant kill names the observer that caught it (termination flip by test_claim_store, field deletion by test_work_record, boundary removal by test_claim_store, parse failure to continue by test_door_adversarial).

metrics.would_require: A timed trial with real reviewers, each shown one delivery and asked to accept or reject, scored against a seeded ground truth of which deliveries were defective. Nothing on this estate runs a human trial or stores its ground truth. The nearest existing thing is scripts/test_acceptance_compression.py, which counts what the receipt puts under REVIEW FIRST, never whether a person then decided correctly.

rules: Zero false PASS. One unit reported PASS whose check does not discriminate the behaviour fails the whole gauntlet, whatever the other numbers say.
Every unverifiable unit reads NO-DATA by name. A missing verdict silently absent from the report counts as a false PASS.
Per changed file, the record names the check that covered it. A changed file with no named check is a miss, counted per file.
The seeded scope drift is reported by scope_audit.py in the record. A drift that lands unremarked fails the gauntlet.
The partial success round must end with a mixed verdict line, not a single word. Both halves are named.
Score is reported per rule, and the raw record is published. No single number stands alone.

win_condition.brother_can_say: this exact behavior failed before the change, passed afterward, this file's test genuinely discriminated the behavior, this second file remains NO-DATA, and this is what you should review first.
win_condition.met_when: Every round's record answers all eleven Zone 1 questions from files on disk, with zero false PASS and every NO-DATA named.

raw_artifacts.rule: Publish raw artifacts. Do not publish only a synthetic score.
